text:
Anna Chen: Quick proposal for a Rollout Observability dashboard — focused on canary vs baseline comparisons and fast drilldowns. Key panels:
- relative delta charts (canary / baseline) for latency (p50/p95) and error rate
- significance ribbon (95% CI) and traffic-weighted sample size indicator
- per-route & per-model-variant breakdowns + customer_tier filter
- annotated timeline with rollout traffic splits & commit hash

Mike Patel: +1. Can we show both absolute and relative views and a ratio chart? Example promQL for p95 by variant:```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, variant))
```
Also flag when sample size < 100 reqs/min so stats aren't noisy.

Sophie Rivera: We should tie guards directly to the rollout spec so the dashboard + alerting use same thresholds. Draft YAML example of the rollout guard:```
rollout: 
  name: model-redwood-3b-v2
  traffic_split: 5
  guards:
    - metric: request_latency_p95_ms
      baseline_comparison: relative_increase
      threshold_pct: 15
      window: 3m
    - metric: error_rate_5xx
      threshold_abs: 0.02
      window: 5m
  rollback_on_alert: true
```
This lets the UI show the active guard set for any rollout.

Tom Liu: For drilldowns we'd want quick filters: region, model_variant, route, customer_tier. Example query to compute relative latency vs baseline:```
(canary_p95{variant="canary"} - baseline_p95{variant="baseline"}) / baseline_p95{variant="baseline"} * 100
```
We should also surface per-route 5xx buckets so SREs can tell if one endpoint is failing.

Mike Patel: Alerting rules idea: page when canary latency > baseline + 20% for 3 consecutive 1m windows AND canary_traffic >= 3% (to avoid noise). Sample alert rule:```
alert: CanaryLatencyRegression
expr: (canary_p95 - baseline_p95) / baseline_p95 > 0.20 and canary_traffic_ratio > 0.03
for: 3m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: "Canary p95 > baseline by >20%"
```
We should route these to the rollout owner channel and also trigger the automatic rollback if rollout.rollback_on_alert is true.

Anna Chen: UX notes — dashboard should let PMs toggle 'relative' vs 'absolute' and annotate the deploy window with commit hash + PR link. Also a small panel showing "Traffic breakdown over time" (stacked) so you can see 5% -> 25% ramp. Add an overlay for config (guards + alert bindings).

Sophie Rivera: Also store a 'golden baseline' snapshot per model-version pair (metrics + vector of recent requests) at the time of canary start. That simplifies comparisons when the baseline drifts.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started — model=redwood-3b@v2 infra=dedicated-us-west traffic=5% commit=9f2c4a2 message="latency-optimizations"

Tom Liu: When canary is live, capture a few trace samples for high-latency requests (e.g., 1/100) and link trace IDs in the latency panel so engineers can jump to traces quickly. Also capture headroom etl (kv cache misses) for model-internal regressions.

Mike Patel: I'll sketch the dashboard panels + alert bindings and open a PR for the metrics panels and the rollout-guard linking. Tagging @Anna for UX :eyes:

Anna Chen: Thanks — once the PR is up I'll run a quick hallway review with SRE/PMs and then we can test on a low-risk canary.
